title: Interleaved retries causing double billing inside burst windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We are seeing customers charged twice for token usage when requests are retried across route/model variants within the same burst window. Root cause appears to be that retries are recorded as independent consumption events in the accounting pipeline before dedup/merge logic runs, and our burst-window enforcer counts both events separately. This manifests for traffic patterns that do fast client retries (100–500ms) and for router-level automatic fallbacks (cheap model -> fallback larger model).

Why this is critical: This leads to both over-billing (customers reported unexpected spikes) and premature burst exhaustion which then causes valid traffic to be throttled. It also pollutes our billing reconciliations with transient duplicates that are hard to reconcile and can trigger SLA disputes.

Observed:
- Example customer (org_id: org_7aK) saw a +30% delta in billed tokens for a 3-hour window on 2026-02-28 coincident with a rollout that enabled fallback routing.
- Grafana: rate-limit/burst-window/charges shows concurrent charge events where the same request_id prefix appears twice with <200ms separation but different route variants.
- Logs: router emitted two downstream calls: /v1/generate@model-small (200ms) then /v1/generate@model-large (500ms). Accounting pipeline treated both as final and incremented the per-key burst counter twice.

Expected:
- Retries or fallback attempts that are causal duplicates should not cause multiple burst-window charges for the same logical client request. We should count the request once (apply idempotency/dedupe semantics within the short dedupe window) or attribute excess cost to fallback policy in a controlled manner (e.g., retroactive replacement rather than additive counting).

Reproduction steps:
1) Configure a route with primary model A (fast/cheap) and fallback B (slower/expensive) with router-level automatic fallback enabled.
2) Use a client that retries on 200–300ms timeouts and/or simulate router fallback by forcing a small failure injection on A.
3) Send steady traffic from a single API key at ~10 qps for 1 minute.
4) Observe accounting stream (kafka topic: accounting.events) and PerKeyBurst counters in Redis.
5) Notice that for the same client request_id prefix (client-generated idempotency key), two accounting records exist and PerKeyBurst was incremented twice within the same 1s burst window.

Initial diagnosis notes: 
- The accounting ingestion path is eventually consistent and receives events from both the router and the per-model billing shim. Router emits immediate event when request is dispatched. Model shim emits final token tally when generation finishes. If both events are ingested before dedupe runs, they both increment the burst counter.
- Dedupe currently operates at the end of the accounting pipeline and is keyed by full request_id; however router uses a different short-lived request_id and the final token report uses the canonical request_id, so dedupe misses.
- Burst-window enforcement is implemented in the rate-policy component which subscribes to the raw accounting events and applies sliding-window increments without consulting the dedupe layer.

Mitigations already applied: 
- Rollback of the fallback rollout to reduce customer impact (completed 2026-03-02).
- Short-term alert created for burst-rate anomalies: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/alerts/burst-rate-anomalies (silenced for internal testing).

Proposed fixes (priority order):
1) Router-level: propagate canonical idempotency/request_id into fallback/secondary calls so both router event and final model event share the same id. Short-term change: attach header X-Canonical-Request-Id.
2) Accounting pipeline: add an early-stage lightweight dedupe that normalizes request identifiers (strip router prefixes, map canonical IDs) and emits a single unified accounting write for items observed within a 2s dedupe window.
3) Rate-policy enforcer: query dedupe cache before incrementing burst counters, or move enforcement to subscribe to the normalized accounting stream rather than raw dispatch events.
4) Retro-billing reconciliation job: identify duplicate-charge groups and emit credits for affected customers for the incident window (run once after fix deploy).

Acceptance criteria: 
- No duplicate per-key burst increments for the same canonical request within a 2s window in staging load tests.
- End-to-end integration test that simulates router dispatch + fallback + model shim results in a single accounting record.
- Retro-billing script identifies and marks duplicates; ops run issues credits for confirmed duplicates.
- No regression in throughput/latency of the accounting pipeline beyond a 10% degradation in p95 processing time.

Implementation notes: 
- Add mapping table in the accounting ingestor that can normalise router-prefixed IDs to canonical IDs (use a Redis LRU for ~60s). Keep it small and short-lived to avoid memory blowup.
- Update router proto to include canonical_request_id optional field (backfill on router > accounting shim compatibility).
- Update unit tests for rate-policy to replay accounting event pairs and ensure idempotent counting.
- Add an e2e harness that replays kafka accounting events into a staging rate-policy process to validate fix.

Links & artifacts: 
- Incident Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/incident/ENG-40567
- Accounting topic sample: kafka://prod/accounting.events (sample exported to s3://redwood-dumps/ENG-40567/)
- Draft PR for early dedupe (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1178
- Retro-billing ticket (ops): https://confluence.redwood.example/display/BILL/ENG-40567-retro-credit-plan

Risks & trade-offs:
- Early-stage dedupe introduces a short detection window which could, in rare race cases, suppress legitimate distinct rapid-fire requests if clients reuse id keys incorrectly. We mitigate by keeping window short (2s) and exposing metrics for suppressed events.
- Adding lookups before enforcement increases enforcer latency. We'll benchmark and add caching to keep p95 within SLO.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy router change that adds canonical_request_id header (canary to 5% traffic) - 2 days testing.
2) Deploy accounting early-dedupe service in front of enforcer in staging and run load tests (3 days).
3) Deploy to canary prod region (10% traffic) and run reconciliation checks (2 days).
4) Full rollout and run retro-billing script for the incident window.

Future improvements (stretch):
- Use token-level attribution instead of event-level increments so partial generations replace earlier counts rather than add.
- Standardize a single request_id across full trace (router -> runtime -> model shim -> accounting) via trace context propagation.
observed_behavior: Accounting increments twice for the same logical request when router dispatch + model final report both appear before dedupe. PerKeyBurst counter shows double increment inside the burst window.
expected_behavior: Single accounting increment per logical request; retries/fallbacks should either dedupe or produce a replace (not additive) event.
mitigation: Roll back fallback rollout (done). Short-term alerting active. Apply canary flags to reduce traffic through fallback routes until fix deployed.
acceptance_criteria: (see description: single accounting record in staging + no duplicate burst increments + retro billing run)
implementation_notes: (see description). Use Redis LRU for id mapping, update router header, add early dedupe stage, add e2e test harness.
